Q: How to change Ruby version when running git hooks in IDEA? A:

IntelliJ inherits the environment variables from the shell instance it was started in. If you run the IDE via GUI, it will inherit the variables from the parent process like file explorer in Windows, display manager in Linux, etc. It is recommended to run the IDE using the terminal instance that contains the necessary environment variables.

https://youtrack.jetbrains.com/articles/SUPPORT-A-1837

Q: Split a query with too many arguments in SQLAlchemy A:

The functions from other answers are extremely slow. The proper way to bulk insert is just to call session.execute(insert(MyTable), data) instead of session.execute(insert(MyTable).values(data)).

Source: https://github.com/sqlalchemy/sqlalchemy/discussions/10537#discussioncomment-7374198

Q: How to merge N DataFrames into one, while using first DF as reference? A:

It seems simple enough to write a simple demo of what I think you want.

  1. You are describing an outer join behaviour. So merge works.
  2. NaN = 0, so na.fill(0) works here.
import pandas as pd
from functools import reduce

# lets make some dummy data.
 dfs = [
     pd.DataFrame({"Object": [1, 2, 3], "dataset1": [1, 2, 3]}),
     pd.DataFrame({"Object": [2, 3, 4], "dataset2": [4, 5, 6]}),
     pd.DataFrame({"Object": [1, 4],    "dataset3": [7, 8]}),
     pd.DataFrame({"Object": [3, 5],    "dataset4": [9, 10]}),
     pd.DataFrame({"Object": [2, 5, 6], "dataset5": [0, 1, 2]}),
 ]

# Here we use reduce to and lambda to 'loop'
result = reduce(lambda l, r: l.merge(r, on="Object", how="outer"),dfs)

# And finally filling NaNs with 0
result_final = result.fillna(0)

Q: Rename MEASUREMENT A:

Here is how I did it with flux:

Start docker playground

docker run -d --name influxdb -p 8086:8086 \
    -e DOCKER_INFLUXDB_INIT_MODE=setup \
    -e DOCKER_INFLUXDB_INIT_USERNAME=dev \
    -e DOCKER_INFLUXDB_INIT_PASSWORD=sjtijlkwjafwe \
    -e DOCKER_INFLUXDB_INIT_ORG=my-org \
    -e DOCKER_INFLUXDB_INIT_BUCKET=my-bucket \
    -e DOCKER_INFLUXDB_INIT_ADMIN_TOKEN=token-43759230840923 \
    influxdb:2.7.11-alpine

Write example data

curl --request POST "http://localhost:8086/api/v2/write?org=my-org&bucket=my-bucket&precision=s" \
    --header "Authorization: Token token-43759230840923" \
    --header "Content-Type: text/plain; charset=utf-8" \
    --data-binary '
        old_measurement,t1=a,t2=q temp=21.1,hum=35.9 1641024000
        old_measurement,t1=b temp=23.0,hum=36.2 1641024000
        old_measurement,t2=w temp=22.4,hum=36.0 1641024000
        old_measurement,t1=a,t2=w temp=22.4,hum=36.0 1641024000
    '

Query

curl --request POST "http://localhost:8086/api/v2/query?org=my-org" \
    --header "Authorization: Token token-43759230840923" \
    --header "Content-Type: application/vnd.flux" \
    --data-binary '
    from(bucket: "my-bucket")
        |> range(start: 0)
        |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "old_measurement")
    '

Shows 8 points

Copy with changed measurement name

curl --request POST "http://localhost:8086/api/v2/query?org=my-org" \
    --header "Authorization: Token token-43759230840923" \
    --header "Content-Type: application/vnd.flux" \
    --data-binary '
    from(bucket: "my-bucket")
        |> range(start: -100y)
        |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "old_measurement")
        |> set(key: "_measurement", value: "new_measurement")
        |> to(bucket: "my-bucket")
        |> limit(n: 0)
    '

It seems you can also do |> map(fn: (r) => ({ r with _measurement: "new_measurement" })) instead of set.

Limiting the response to 0 potentially makes it faster, because it avoids sending the whole database to your client.

Query new measurement

curl --request POST "http://localhost:8086/api/v2/query?org=my-org" \
    --header "Authorization: Token token-43759230840923" \
    --header "Content-Type: application/vnd.flux" \
    --data-binary '
    from(bucket: "my-bucket")
        |> range(start: 0)
        |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "new_measurement")
    '

Shows the same 8 points

Delete old data

curl --request POST "http://localhost:8086/api/v2/delete?org=my-org&bucket=my-bucket" \
    --header "Authorization: Token token-43759230840923" \
    --header "Content-Type: application/json" \
    --data '{
        "start": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
        "stop": "2030-01-01T00:00:00Z",
        "predicate": "_measurement=\"old_measurement\""
    }'

If you query again, you should see no data for the old measurement.
